result.title: From Complex Histories to Simple Predictors: Predictive Dimension in Dynamic Graph Learning
result.summary: Existing continuous-time graph learning methods rely heavily on complex neural architectures to encode ever-expanding interaction histories. However, the future conditional distribution induced by complex histories can often be characterized by a low-dimensional predictive state manifold, implying that only a few predictive degrees of freedom are essential for future interactions. We therefore argue that continuous-time graph learning should identify low-dimensional states sufficient for future prediction rather than reconstruct the full history. To make this perspective measurable, we define and independently estimate the intrinsic predictive dimension, which quantifies the effective predictive degrees of freedom required by a given task. Specifically, we remove the history-independent marginal from the history-conditioned future distribution, decompose the resulting predictive residual operator, and estimate the minimum effective rank needed to preserve the predictive power of the full history. Experiments across datasets show that model performance saturation is largely determined by the intrinsic predictive dimension. Based on this finding, we propose PreDyG, a lightweight model whose capacity is matched to the intrinsic predictive dimension. PreDyG achieves superior predictive performance with only 0.07\% of the parameters of a representative complex baseline.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张连续时间图学习应识别对未来预测充分的低维预测状态，而非重建完整交互历史；为此定义并独立估计任务的内在预测维度（去除历史无关边际后分解预测残差算子，取保留全历史预测力所需的最小有效秩），并据此提出容量与之匹配的轻量模型 PreDyG。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用预测残差算子的有效秩量化「未来预测所需自由度」并提供容量匹配思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 工作区的维度选择与所需信息是否充分提供可核查的度量线索；但领域为时序图，迁移到 VLM 推理尚待确认。
